# KS-1145 A-SLUGONLYDRIFT-R16B ADD ONE CELL TO THE ks949 REAL-POSTGRESQL SUITE — AG7: a SLUG-ONLY tenant drift on a second id is repaired by the guard's `tenant_slug` arm (`UPDATE 1`, slug restored) — the coverage note CN-2 of the #973 gate (a one-arm `IS DISTINCT FROM` guard was invisible to the suite) — Wednesday's task for Ornith, TEST_ONLY, **ONE existing bash suite, ONE pure-insertion hunk, no product file** (written 2026-09-22 16:0x by the feed15 drafter; the ticket's item 2; item 1 (CN-1, ID3's capture-size assertion) is NOT in this brief — part B, tabled)

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`
Tip: `3bad652d17cf111c1e2e1bed1ae7686894637487`
Farm: `shared+tsx`

Written from develop `3bad652d17cf111c1e2e1bed1ae7686894637487` (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/develop` at 15:54 on 2026-09-22, read verbs only). The suite at that tip is **376 lines** (last change `818002259`, 2026-09-13, #973), read whole; its full content is in `files[...]` of your input. The product it judges is `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` (last change `778e6cfe2`, 2026-09-21): the two-arm re-sync guard at **`:1043`** `AND (u.tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM v.tenant_id::uuid OR u.tenant_slug IS DISTINCT FROM v.tenant_slug)` — the suite EXTRACTS that statement from the product source at `:125-:130` (awk over `mainPool.query(`), so a tamper on `:1043` is what every cell runs. Runner: **bash** (a `*.test.sh` suite, run by the checker as `/bin/bash <file>` from the clone root, bash 3.2.57). **The suite needs the workspace install and the shared build** (`:113-:114` `die`, not SKIP: `packages/shared/dist/index.js` and `node_modules/.bin/tsx`) — the `Farm:` line above tells the harness to farm them into the scratch clone before the suite runs (the 2026-09-22 opt-in; without it the bare clone dies at `:113`). A real PostgreSQL 15/18 from a Homebrew keg is started by the suite itself, unix-socket only, in its own mkdtemps (`:161-:184`); no TCP port is bound, and the live postgres on this box (`127.0.0.1:5432`) is never touched.

## THE MODE — read this twice

**TEST_ONLY.** Your diff touches EXACTLY ONE file: the suite above, MODIFIED IN PLACE (`--- a/<path>` / `+++ b/<path>`, the path exactly as written above). You never touch `startup-migrations.ts` or any other file: no product behaviour changes; ONE cell (AG7) is ADDED between AG5 and AG6, inside the auth-then-gateway section.

## What the change does (one paragraph)

Section 8 of the suite (`:286-:301`, "AG: auth-then-gateway") seeds the twelve users with auth's real `seedDemoUsers`, plants a drift on the contested id `...060` at `:291` — on BOTH columns (`tenant_slug='ks949-stale-slug'` AND `tenant_id='...dead'`) — and AG4 (`:296-:297`) asserts the statement re-syncs it. Because BOTH columns drift, a guard with only the `tenant_id` arm (`AND (u.tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM v.tenant_id::uuid)`) still matches the row and the `SET` repairs both columns: the #973 gate's Tg3 tamper (the slug arm deleted) read `27 passed, 0 failed` — CN-2. Only a drift on the slug ALONE tells the two arms apart: the shipped guard reads `UPDATE 1` (the gate's R5 control), a one-arm guard reads `UPDATE 0` and the drift stays. AG7 plants exactly that on a SECOND id, `c1000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` (james.wilson, oxford-university — the second VALUES row of the statement at `:1030`), runs the extracted statement once more, and asserts BOTH the command tag `UPDATE 1` and the slug read back as `oxford-university`; then it puts the slug back by a direct UPDATE so every later cell (AG6's count, ID1-ID3's captures, the controls) sees the table exactly as it would without AG7 — ID2 compares the `:293` snapshot `$A` with the post-idempotence snapshot, and the restore keeps them equal under every arm. `TOTAL_CELLS` at `:82` is NOT changed in this brief: the tally line prints `(of 27 cells)` while 28 cells print `ok`; the checker counts printed cells, not the constant (part B carries `27 -> 28` with CN-1 — said plainly in the raise notes).

## The exact change — ONE hunk in the suite

A PURE INSERTION of 12 `+` lines between `:299` (the AG5 line, leading context) and `:300` (`N12=$(COUNT12 ag); ...`, trailing context) — both unique in the file, both ASCII. Copy every line byte for byte. Every `+` line is ASCII only, carries NO backslash, NO backtick, no `printf`, no bash-4 idiom (`[ ]`, `$( )`, a here-string `<<<` as the suite's own `PSQL` calls use at `:291`, `ok`/`bad` as at `:85-:86`). The three `#` lines are comments and stay. `$STMT`, `$ID0001`, `$OUT7`, `$SL7` are plain `$name` expansions inside double quotes — no `${}`, no arithmetic. There is no blank line anywhere in the fence. **Your diff MUST begin with the two file-header lines, above the `@@` line: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh` then `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`.**

```
@@ -299,2 +299,14 @@
 [ "$NB" = "$NA" ] && ok "AG5: names, role and status untouched on all 12 rows" || bad "AG5: the statement changed names, role or status"
+# KS-1145 (CN-2 of the #973 gate): a SLUG-ONLY drift on a second id. AG4's drift is on BOTH
+# columns, so a guard with only the tenant_id arm still repairs it; a drift on the slug alone
+# is the one the tenant_slug arm of the guard (startup-migrations.ts:1043) exists for.
+ID0001="c1000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
+PSQL ag <<<"UPDATE users SET tenant_slug='ks949-slug-only-drift' WHERE id='$ID0001';" >/dev/null
+OUT7=$(PSQL ag <<<"$STMT"); SL7=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT tenant_slug FROM users WHERE id='$ID0001';")
+if [ "$OUT7" = "UPDATE 1" ] && [ "$SL7" = "oxford-university" ]; then
+  ok "AG7: a slug-only drift on ...0001 is repaired by the guard's tenant_slug arm (UPDATE 1, slug restored)"
+else
+  bad "AG7: a slug-only drift on ...0001 is NOT repaired - command tag '$OUT7', slug reads '$SL7' (the guard's tenant_slug arm is gone or inert)"
+fi
+PSQL ag <<<"UPDATE users SET tenant_slug='oxford-university' WHERE id='$ID0001';" >/dev/null
 N12=$(COUNT12 ag); NT=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT count(*) FROM users;")
```

Do NOT touch `:291` (AG4's both-column drift), `:296-:297` (AG4), `:300-:301` (AG6), section 9 (`:303-:318`, ID1-ID3), `TOTAL_CELLS` at `:82`, or the controls. Do NOT add a `printf`. Do NOT rename the cell: the checker names it by the literal prefix `AG7:`.

## Tampers

Both tampers are ONE-line edits of the product's guard at `startup-migrations.ts:1043` (the `From` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file as a whole line — python whole-line scan: 1 hit at 1043). The suite reads the statement FROM the product source (`:125-:130`), so the tampered guard is what `$STMT` carries in every cell. The checker plants each and restores the file by bytes (T8).

### SLUGARMGONE — the guard keeps only its tenant_id arm (the #973 gate's Tg3, the tamper CN-2 says the suite cannot see): AG4's both-column drift is still repaired (green), a slug-only drift is not

```

To:

### GUARDINERT — the guard is made always-true (`OR true`): every boot rewrites all twelve rows, so ID3's no-change run reads UPDATE 12 and AG7's slug-only run reads UPDATE 12, not UPDATE 1
File: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`
Line: 1043

- `ag6`

*(All are literal prefixes of the descriptions the suite prints — `GA1:` `:275`, `AG4:` `:297`, `AG6:` `:301`, `SRC1:` `:340-:341`, `ID3:` `:315`/`:317`; each prefix names exactly one cell (the `ok` and `bad` lines of a cell share it). Under GUARDINERT: AG4 green (everything is rewritten, the drift included), AG6 green, SRC1 green (the statement is still an UPDATE naming no PII column); ID3 red at the tip already (its purpose) and AG7 red (UPDATE 12).)*

## THE CHANGE — state it to yourself before you write a line

At the untouched tip the suite is `27 passed, 0 failed (of 27 cells)`, rc 0 (measured on the farmed scratch clone, PostgreSQL 15.14). With this hunk: `28 passed, 0 failed (of 27 cells)`, rc 0 — AG7 green (`UPDATE 1`, slug `oxford-university`). Under **SLUGARMGONE** with this hunk: AG7 red (`command tag 'UPDATE 0', slug reads 'ks949-slug-only-drift'`), every other cell green, `27 passed, 1 failed`, rc 1. Under **GUARDINERT** with this hunk: AG7 red (`command tag 'UPDATE 12'`) and ID3 red (`command tag 'UPDATE 12', 12 of 12 updated_at moved`), `26 passed, 2 failed`, rc 1. Under SLUGARMGONE WITHOUT this hunk: `27 passed, 0 failed` — the blindness the ticket names (measured by the #973 gate as Tg3, 0 red). All reds are assertion reds (no bash diagnostic).

- **No backslash** in any `+` line (0, counted); **no backtick** (0); **no non-ASCII** (0); no bash-4 idiom; the suite after the fence parses (`bash -n` rc 0).
- **Premise: the surface.** A shell suite that starts its own PostgreSQL over a unix socket in `mktemp -d` dirs and removes them on EXIT (`:168-:173`); nothing outside `$TMPDIR` and the clone is written. Not an auth surface.

Every one of the 12 `+` lines is its OWN physical line (the INPUT JSON shows this brief's line breaks as the two characters backslash and n inside a JSON string — DECODE them; a `+` line that carries a backslash is a FAIL).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# KS-962 / KS-950 — the api-gateway's per-client user statement, executed against
# a REAL PostgreSQL alongside auth's REAL seeder, in BOTH orders.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` used to INSERT twelve users
# with `ON CONFLICT (email)`. Two defects hid in that one statement:
#
#   1. On the deployed schema (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`) `users.email` is
#      `TEXT NOT NULL` with NO unique index — uniqueness lives on
#      `email_lookup_hash`, because non-deterministic encryption cannot enforce
#      it — so `ON CONFLICT (email)` raised 42P10 on EVERY boot and the
#      statement never seeded anything. Its failure was logged at debug, a
#      level the demo does not read. (KS-950, KS-962.)
#   2. The fix that was tried first — repoint the target to the primary key —
#      made the statement RUN, and running it was worse: it wrote PLAINTEXT into
#      `users.email`, where every real row is AES-GCM ciphertext, and never set
#      `email_lookup_hash`, the column the login path looks users up by.
#      Reverted out of #885; recorded in KS-962 as "what not to do". PR #928
#      re-landed that shape and is superseded by the round this suite ships in.
#
# THE CONTRACT (KS-962, ratified 2026-09-07): the statement creates NO row under
# any condition; it may change only `tenant_id` / `tenant_slug` (and
# `updated_at`), only on rows whose `id` already exists; it never names `email`,
# `email_lookup_hash`, the names, `role` or `status`. Auth's `seedDemoUsers`
# owns the twelve.
#
# WHAT THIS SUITE DOES ABOUT IT (the contract KS-962 sets for its return):
#   - drives BOTH seeders — auth's real `seedDemoUsers` over tsx, and the
#     gateway statement EXTRACTED FROM THE PRODUCT SOURCE (sha256 printed; a
#     restated copy would drift, pass, and prove nothing about what ships) —
#     against ONE real database, in BOTH orders;
#   - on the DEPLOYED shape: `docker/init/*.sql` + `migrations/*.sql` applied
#     from the repo's own files (auth's seeder needs migration 039's
#     `auth_find_user_by_email_hash`; a users-table-only shape seeds 0 rows and
#     was measured doing so);
#   - does NOT stub `isEncryptedPii` — the REAL one from `packages/shared/dist`
#     is what judges every email;
#   - carries CONTROL-A (the reverted #928 form CREATES twelve plaintext rows
#     with no hash — the cells that must catch it are shown catching it) and
#     CONTROL-B (the develop `ON CONFLICT (email)` form fails 42P10 on this
#     shape — the harness reproduces the defect, it does not pass everything);
#   - drives the real `runStartupMigrations()` twice to prove the loader half
#     of KS-950: a failing file migration is reported INCOMPLETE at warn, and a
#     failing re-sync is logged at warn, not debug.
#
# THE DATABASE. A real PostgreSQL from a Homebrew keg (or a Linux package
# directory), started UNIX-SOCKET ONLY in this test's own mkdtemps:
# `listen_addresses=''`, no port, no slot, no container, no Docker. Discovery
# order: KS949_PG_BIN, then the keg paths below — never PATH alone, so a
# LIVE postgres on this machine (Homebrew's `postgresql@15` service listening on
# 127.0.0.1:5432 was found running on the dev box; not ours) is never touched:
# every connection here names THIS test's socket directory and port number.
# The socket path is capped at ~103 bytes by the OS, so the socket dir is a
# short mkdtemp under $TMPDIR; the data dir can be anywhere.
#
# WHEN THERE IS NO POSTGRESQL. Prints one SKIP line naming the reason, the
# directories searched and `0/N cells run`, and exits 0 — a push from a box
# without a keg is not refused (ruled 2026-09-13). The runner counts an exit-0
# suite as passed; the SKIP line is the honest signal until the runner carries
# a skip tally (ticketed). A missing tsx or an unbuilt packages/shared is a
# FAIL, not a SKIP: the pre-push preflight already requires both.
#
# COST: measured 2026-09-13 on an M-series Mac, PostgreSQL 15.14: 5-18 s
# (first cold run 18 s; typically 5-9 s: initdb ~1 s, one schema build ~2 s
# copied by TEMPLATE, two seeder runs ~2 s each, two boots ~1 s each).
# Printed on every run.
#
# Needs: bash 3.2+, node, the workspace install (tsx), packages/shared built.

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DEV_DIR="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
SRC="$DEV_DIR/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts"
AUTH_REPO="$DEV_DIR/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts"
SHARED_DIST="$DEV_DIR/packages/shared/dist/index.js"
TSX="$DEV_DIR/node_modules/.bin/tsx"
PGPORT_NAME=54329          # only ever a socket FILE name: no TCP is bound
TOTAL_CELLS=27   # KS-962 round 2: +ID3, the IS DISTINCT FROM guard's regression cell

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()  { PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  ok   — $1"; }
bad() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL — $1"; }
# KS-950 round 2 (P3): an abort used to print a hard-coded `0 passed` after
# cells had already passed; the summary now carries the real tallies.
die() { echo "  FAIL — $1"; echo "  $PASS passed, $((FAIL+1)) failed (of $TOTAL_CELLS cells) — aborted"; exit 1; }
sha() { if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1; else sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; fi; }
one_line() { tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-"${1:-140}"; }

echo "ks949_main_seed_idempotence:"
T_ALL=$(date +%s)

# --- 1. PostgreSQL discovery: env override, then known package dirs, never PATH alone ---
PG_CANDIDATES="${KS949_PG_BIN:-} /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@15/bin /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@18/bin /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@16/bin /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql/bin /usr/local/opt/postgresql@15/bin /usr/local/opt/postgresql/bin /usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin /usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin"
PGBIN=""
for d in $PG_CANDIDATES; do
  [ -n "$d" ] || continue
  if [ -x "$d/initdb" ] && [ -x "$d/pg_ctl" ] && [ -x "$d/postgres" ] && [ -x "$d/psql" ]; then PGBIN="$d"; break; fi
done
if [ -z "$PGBIN" ]; then
  echo "  SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; searched: $(printf '%s' "$PG_CANDIDATES" | tr -s ' ' ' '); 0/$TOTAL_CELLS cells run"
  echo "  (set KS949_PG_BIN=<dir with initdb pg_ctl postgres psql> to run this suite)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "  postgres: $("$PGBIN/postgres" --version 2>/dev/null | one_line 60) from $PGBIN"

# --- 2. Preconditions that FAIL, not skip ---
[ -f "$SRC" ]        || die "product source not found: $SRC"
[ -f "$AUTH_REPO" ]  || die "auth seeder source not found: $AUTH_REPO"
[ -f "$SHARED_DIST" ] || die "packages/shared is not built ($SHARED_DIST missing) — run: npm run build -w packages/shared"
[ -x "$TSX" ]        || die "tsx not installed at $TSX — run: npm ci"
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "node not on PATH"
[ -f "$DEV_DIR/docker/init/01-schema.sql" ] || die "docker/init/01-schema.sql not found"
[ -d "$DEV_DIR/migrations" ] || die "migrations/ not found"

# --- 3. The statement, extracted from the product source ----------------------
# The seed block is the `mainPool.query(` template literal that FOLLOWS the
# "Main DB migrations" summary line inside runStartupMigrations (an earlier
# `mainPool.query(` provisions the secuura_app role and is not it). Taken from
# `await mainPool.query(\`` up to the closing `\`);` line, whatever form it
# currently has — so the cells always judge what ships.
STMT=$(awk '
  /Main DB migrations/ { m=1 }
  m && !f && /await mainPool\.query\(`/ { f=1; sub(/.*await mainPool\.query\(`/, ""); }
  f && /^[[:space:]]*`\);/ { exit }
  f { print }
' "$SRC")
[ -n "$STMT" ] || die "could not extract the main-DB user statement from $SRC (no mainPool.query template literal found)"
echo "  statement extracted from product source, sha256 $(printf '%s' "$STMT" | sha)"

# The twelve ids come from the statement itself, so this suite cannot drift
# from the rows the product names. Each VALUES row starts with a quoted uuid.
IDS_LIST=$(printf '%s\n' "$STMT" | grep -oE "^[[:space:]]*\('[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}'" | grep -oE "[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")
IDS_N=$(printf '%s\n' "$IDS_LIST" | grep -c .)
IDS_SQL=$(printf '%s\n' "$IDS_LIST" | sed "s/^/'/; s/$/'/" | paste -sd, -)
if [ "$IDS_N" = "12" ]; then ok "the statement names exactly 12 user ids (derived from source, not typed here)"; else bad "expected 12 ids in the statement's VALUES, found $IDS_N"; fi

# --- 4. A real PostgreSQL, unix socket only, in this test's own mkdtemps ------
# KS-950 round 2 (P3): the trap is installed BEFORE the mkdtemps. It used to
# come after the socket-cap check, so a cap die (or a failed second mktemp)
# left empty dirs behind whatever KS949_KEEP said. cleanup() only touches
# what exists: it stops postgres only once PG_UP=1 and removes (or keeps)
# only the dirs that were created.
DATA=""; SOCK=""; WORK=""; PG_UP=0
cleanup() {
  if [ "$PG_UP" = 1 ]; then "$PGBIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA/db" -w -m fast stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  if [ "${KS949_KEEP:-}" = 1 ]; then echo "  (KS949_KEEP=1: kept $DATA $SOCK $WORK)"; return; fi
  for d in "$DATA" "$SOCK" "$WORK"; do [ -n "$d" ] && rm -rf "$d"; done
}
trap cleanup EXIT
DATA=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks949data.XXXXXX") || die "mktemp failed"
SOCK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks949sock.XXXXXX") || die "mktemp failed"
WORK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks949work.XXXXXX") || die "mktemp failed"
[ "${#SOCK}" -le 88 ] || die "socket directory path too long for a unix socket (${#SOCK} chars: $SOCK); set TMPDIR to a short path"

"$PGBIN/initdb" -D "$DATA/db" -U ks949 -A trust --no-locale -E UTF8 >"$WORK/initdb.log" 2>&1 \
  || die "initdb failed: $(tail -3 "$WORK/initdb.log" | one_line 200)"
"$PGBIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA/db" -l "$WORK/pg.log" -w \
  -o "-c listen_addresses='' -k '$SOCK' -p $PGPORT_NAME -c fsync=off -c synchronous_commit=off -c full_page_writes=off" \
  start >"$WORK/start.log" 2>&1 || die "postgres did not start: $(tail -3 "$WORK/pg.log" | one_line 200)"
PG_UP=1

PSQL() { "$PGBIN/psql" -h "$SOCK" -p $PGPORT_NAME -U ks949 -d "$1" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -tA 2>&1; }
PSQLF() { "$PGBIN/psql" -h "$SOCK" -p $PGPORT_NAME -U ks949 -d "$1" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f "$2"; }
DB_URL() { printf 'postgresql://ks949@/%s?host=%s&port=%s' "$1" "$SOCK" "$PGPORT_NAME"; }

# The instance must be reachable ONLY through this test's socket. A control that
# cannot fail is not a control, so the negative side is asserted too.
LA=$(PSQL postgres <<<"SELECT '[' || current_setting('listen_addresses') || ']';")
if [ "$LA" = "[]" ]; then ok "postgres is unix-socket only (listen_addresses=[], socket dir is this test's mkdtemp)"; else bad "listen_addresses is $LA, expected []"; fi
if "$PGBIN/psql" -h "$SOCK/no-such-dir" -p $PGPORT_NAME -U ks949 -d postgres -tAc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then bad "CONTROL: a wrong socket dir still connected — the socket check cannot fail"; else ok "CONTROL: a wrong socket dir does not connect (the socket check can fail)"; fi

# --- 5. The DEPLOYED shape, once, from the repo's own files; copied per cell ---
# docker/init/*.sql in entrypoint order, minus 00-* (it creates the PLATFORM
# database over dblink — not this database's shape) and the *.sh (platform DB,
# app role — the role is created here NOLOGIN so RLS grants apply); then the
# runner's tracker table; then migrations/*.sql routed as
# scripts/run-migrations.sh routes them (any *platform* file goes to the
# platform database, which this suite has no need of).
TEMPLATE=ks949_template
PSQL postgres <<<"CREATE DATABASE $TEMPLATE;" >/dev/null
PSQL "$TEMPLATE" <<<"DO \$\$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='secuura_app') THEN CREATE ROLE secuura_app NOLOGIN; END IF; END \$\$;" >/dev/null
: >"$WORK/schema.log"
INIT_N=0   # KS-950 round 2 (P4): "01-08" is a prefix range, not a count — print the count too
for f in "$DEV_DIR"/docker/init/0[1-9]*.sql; do
  PSQLF "$TEMPLATE" "$f" >>"$WORK/schema.log" 2>&1 || die "docker/init load failed at $(basename "$f"): $(tail -2 "$WORK/schema.log" | one_line 200)"
  INIT_N=$((INIT_N+1))
done
PSQL "$TEMPLATE" <<<"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _secuura_migrations (filename TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW());" >/dev/null
MIG_N=0
for f in "$DEV_DIR"/migrations/*.sql; do
  case "$(basename "$f")" in *platform*|*Platform*) continue ;; esac
  PSQLF "$TEMPLATE" "$f" >>"$WORK/schema.log" 2>&1 || die "migration failed at $(basename "$f"): $(tail -2 "$WORK/schema.log" | one_line 200)"
  MIG_N=$((MIG_N+1))
done
echo "  deployed shape built: docker/init 01-08 ($INIT_N files) + $MIG_N main-DB migrations (template $TEMPLATE)"
mkdb() { PSQL postgres <<<"CREATE DATABASE $1 TEMPLATE $TEMPLATE;" >/dev/null; }

# --- 6. The seeders --------------------------------------------------------------
# auth's REAL seedDemoUsers, imported from source over tsx. Sentinels only:
# fixed hex keys, fixed non-secret passwords, a hashFn that produces a string
# no verifier accepts (bcrypt/argon2 hashes begin '$'; this cannot).
cat >"$WORK/seed_driver.ts" <<'EOF'
const DEV = process.argv[2];
const shared = require(`${DEV}/node_modules/@secuura/shared`);
shared.initFromEnv();
(async () => {
  const userRepo = await import(`${DEV}/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`);
  const db = await import(`${DEV}/services/auth/src/db.ts`);
  const hashFn = async (pw: string) => `!ks949-sentinel-hash:${pw.length}`;
  await userRepo.seedDemoUsers(hashFn);
  await db.closeDb();
})().catch((e: any) => { console.error('[seed_driver] FAILED', e?.message || e); process.exit(1); });
EOF
SEED() {  # $1 = db name; prints the driver's exit code
  ( cd "$DEV_DIR/services/auth" && env -u PII_PLAINTEXT_CUTOFF -u MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED -u PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL -u ENABLE_DEMO_SEED \
      NODE_ENV=test ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true \
      ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD='ks949-sentinel-not-a-secret' DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD='ks949-sentinel-not-a-secret' \
      PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111 \
      PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY=2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222 \
      DATABASE_URL="$(DB_URL "$1")" \
      "$TSX" "$WORK/seed_driver.ts" "$DEV_DIR" >"$WORK/seed_$1.log" 2>&1 ); echo $?
}
# the gateway's REAL runStartupMigrations(), for the loader half (L1-L3)
cat >"$WORK/boot_driver.ts" <<'EOF'
const DEV = process.argv[2];
(async () => {
  const m = await import(`${DEV}/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`);
  await m.runStartupMigrations();
})().catch((e: any) => { console.error('[boot_driver] FAILED', e?.message || e); process.exit(1); });
EOF
BOOT() {  # $1 = db name, $2 = MIGRATIONS_DIR; output in $WORK/boot_$1.log
  ( cd "$DEV_DIR/services/api-gateway" && env -u MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL -u PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL -u MIGRATION_PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL -u APP_DB_PASSWORD \
      DATABASE_URL="$(DB_URL "$1")" MIGRATIONS_DIR="$2" \
      "$TSX" "$WORK/boot_driver.ts" "$DEV_DIR" >"$WORK/boot_$1.log" 2>&1 ); echo $?
}

SNAP() { PSQL "$1" <<<"SELECT id,email,email_lookup_hash,first_name,last_name,role,status,tenant_id,tenant_slug FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL) ORDER BY id;"; }
EMAILHASH() { PSQL "$1" <<<"SELECT id||'|'||email||'|'||coalesce(email_lookup_hash,'<null>') FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL) ORDER BY id;"; }
ENC_OK() {  # "<n>/<t>" of the twelve whose email passes the REAL isEncryptedPii — not a stub
  PSQL "$1" <<<"SELECT email FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL);" | node -e "
    const { isEncryptedPii } = require(process.argv[1]); let n = 0, t = 0;
    require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).forEach(e => { t++; if (isEncryptedPii(e)) n++; });
    console.log(n + '/' + t);" "$DEV_DIR/packages/shared/dist"
}
COUNT12() { PSQL "$1" <<<"SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL);"; }

# --- 7. GA: gateway statement FIRST, then auth ------------------------------------
echo "  -- GA: gateway-then-auth"
mkdb ga
OUT=$(PSQL ga <<<"$STMT"); N=$(PSQL ga <<<"SELECT count(*) FROM users;")
[ "$N" = "0" ] && ok "GA1: the statement creates NO row on an empty table (count $N)" || bad "GA1: the statement created rows on an empty table (count $N; KS-962: no row may be created)"
rc=$(SEED ga); [ "$rc" = "0" ] && ok "GA2: auth's seedDemoUsers ran after the statement (rc 0)" || bad "GA2: auth's seeder exited $rc: $(tail -2 "$WORK/seed_ga.log" | one_line 200)"
N12=$(COUNT12 ga); NT=$(PSQL ga <<<"SELECT count(*) FROM users;")
[ "$N12" = "12" ] && ok "GA3: auth created all 12 gateway-named rows ($NT rows in total)" || bad "GA3: only $N12 of the 12 gateway-named rows exist after auth ($NT total)"
E=$(ENC_OK ga); [ "$E" = "12/12" ] && ok "GA4: every email of the 12 passes the REAL isEncryptedPii ($E)" || bad "GA4: isEncryptedPii passes $E of the 12 emails"

case "$OUT" in *ERROR*) bad "GA6: the statement errors on the auth-seeded table: $(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 120)" ;; *) ok "GA6: the statement runs on the auth-seeded table without error" ;; esac
[ "$B" = "$A" ] && ok "GA7: the 12 rows are byte-identical across the statement (email, hash, names, role, status, tenant)" || bad "GA7: the statement changed one of the 12 rows"

# --- 8. AG: auth FIRST, then the gateway statement --------------------------------
echo "  -- AG: auth-then-gateway"
mkdb ag
rc=$(SEED ag); [ "$rc" = "0" ] && ok "AG1: auth's seedDemoUsers ran on the empty table (rc 0)" || bad "AG1: auth's seeder exited $rc: $(tail -2 "$WORK/seed_ag.log" | one_line 200)"
# plant a DRIFTED tenant on the contested id (…060): the statement's one job is to re-sync it
PSQL ag <<<"UPDATE users SET tenant_slug='ks949-stale-slug', tenant_id='00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000dead' WHERE id='$ID060';" >/dev/null
BE=$(EMAILHASH ag); B=$(SNAP ag)
OUT=$(PSQL ag <<<"$STMT"); AE=$(EMAILHASH ag); A=$(SNAP ag)
case "$OUT" in *ERROR*) bad "AG2: the statement errors on the seeded table: $(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 120)" ;; *) ok "AG2: the statement runs on the seeded table without error" ;; esac
[ "$BE" = "$AE" ] && ok "AG3: email + email_lookup_hash byte-identical before/after on all 12 rows" || bad "AG3: the statement changed email or email_lookup_hash on an existing row (KS-962: never)"
SL=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT tenant_slug||'|'||tenant_id FROM users WHERE id='$ID060';")
[ "$SL" = "secuura-co|a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000099" ] && ok "AG4: the planted drift on …060 is re-synced to secuura-co / …099" || bad "AG4: …060 reads '$SL' after the statement (expected secuura-co|a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000099)"
NB=$(printf '%s\n' "$B" | cut -d'|' -f4-7); NA=$(printf '%s\n' "$A" | cut -d'|' -f4-7)
[ "$NB" = "$NA" ] && ok "AG5: names, role and status untouched on all 12 rows" || bad "AG5: the statement changed names, role or status"
N12=$(COUNT12 ag); NT=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT count(*) FROM users;")
[ "$N12" = "12" ] && ok "AG6: still exactly 12 gateway-named rows ($NT total) — nothing created" || bad "AG6: $N12 gateway-named rows after the statement ($NT total)"

# --- 9. Idempotence: the statement again on the same database ---------------------
# KS-962 round 2 (ID3): SNAP carries no updated_at, so ID2 stayed green with the
# IS DISTINCT FROM guard deleted (measured by the round-1 gate: 26/26 without
# it). The guard's whole point is that a no-change run writes NOTHING — pinned
# here on the two things only the guard changes: the command tag and updated_at.
UPD_B=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT id||'|'||updated_at FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL) ORDER BY id;")
OUT=$(PSQL ag <<<"$STMT"); A2=$(SNAP ag)
UPD_A=$(PSQL ag <<<"SELECT id||'|'||updated_at FROM users WHERE id IN ($IDS_SQL) ORDER BY id;")
case "$OUT" in *ERROR*) bad "ID1: the second run errors: $(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 120)" ;; *) ok "ID1: the statement runs a second time without error" ;; esac
[ "$A" = "$A2" ] && ok "ID2: the 12 rows are identical after the second run" || bad "ID2: the second run changed a row"
MOVED=$(diff <(printf '%s\n' "$UPD_B") <(printf '%s\n' "$UPD_A") | grep -c '^>')
if [ "$OUT" = "UPDATE 0" ] && [ "$MOVED" = "0" ]; then
  ok "ID3: a no-change second run writes nothing — UPDATE 0 and every updated_at byte-identical (the IS DISTINCT FROM guard)"
else
  bad "ID3: the no-change second run wrote rows — command tag '$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 40)', $MOVED of 12 updated_at moved (the IS DISTINCT FROM guard is gone or inert)"
fi

if [ "$N" = "12" ] && [ "$E" = "0/12" ] && [ "$H" = "0" ]; then

else
  bad "CONTROL-A: the #928 form gave rows=$N encrypted=$E hashes=$H (expected 12 / 0/12 / 0): $(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 100)"
fi
mkdb cb
OUT=$(PSQL cb <<<"$DEVELOP_FORM")
case "$OUT" in
  *"no unique or exclusion constraint"*) ok "CONTROL-B: the develop ON CONFLICT (email) form fails 42P10 on the deployed shape — the harness reproduces the defect" ;;
  *) bad "CONTROL-B: expected 42P10 from the old form, got: $(printf '%s' "$OUT" | one_line 120)" ;;
esac
[ "$N12" = "11" ] && bad "CONTROL-C: 12 and 11 both matched — the count assertion is inert" || ok "CONTROL-C: the row-count assertion discriminates (11 does not match $N12)"

# --- 11. Source-level: the shape and the level, read from the file -------------------
echo "  -- source"
case "$STMT" in
  *"INSERT INTO users"*) bad "SRC1: the shipped statement is an INSERT — KS-962: it must create no row" ;;

esac
